newsitem.title: JAPAN: LME copper seen firm, may consolidate--Mitsubishi.
newsitem.headline: LME copper seen firm, may consolidate--Mitsubishi.

text.p: The downside risk has eased for the near term for London Metal Exchange copper prices, which are likely to hold firm but may consolidate for a while in a range of $1,900-$1,970 per tonne, Mitsubishi Corp said in its latest monthly report on the copper futures market.

The major trading house's report said the threat of options-related selling had declined, while selling pressure from U.S. funds and other speculators appeared to have run its course as technical indicators suggested the market was oversold. Any rallies, however, were likely to be limited to short-covering, so the upside was considered limited.

The report set intermediate-term targets for three-month LME copper at nearby resistance of $1,970, followed by a high of about $2,070 hit on September 3. Three-month copper on the LME was quoted at $1,927/$1,930 on Thursday.
It added that traders were still taking a cautious view of the market despite Sumitomo Corp's announcement last week that it had covered most of its open copper positions.
"Viewed from this perspective, there is a strong possibility that the market will consolidate for a while between $1,900 and $1,970," the report said. -- Tokyo Commodities Desk (81-3-3432-6179)
